feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning in digital communications, web strategy, and platform operations. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it would be more impactful with sharper outcome-focused bullets, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at the National Association of Counties, showing increasing scope, leadership, and responsibility.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is generally polished, concise, and aligned with the target brand of a strategic digital communications leader.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scale: include performance improvements, engagement gains, efficiency savings, revenue/support impact, or adoption results. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than achievements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Minor language/style issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, one or two concrete signals of scale, and slightly less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with current market positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader” rather than “professional.”
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent roles, e.g. enterprise web modernization, 10,000+ page site migration, or multi-channel programs for mission-driven/member organizations.
- Tighten phrasing by replacing “building the workflows and systems that support” with “designing workflows and systems for.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is reinforced throughout Work Experience, so keep it brief here rather than listing multiple adjacent strengths.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, distinctive language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & insight reporting.”
- Group related items and standardize style/pluralization; suggested version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If space is tight, cut lower-priority items like “Web & CMS administration” in favor of more strategic wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Policy & advocacy communication” and “Multimedia & live event production” are already reinforced in Topline Skills and Work Experience.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale to distinguish it from your NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-led bullet: “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more outcome-focused: include number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, or speed/efficiency gains if available.
- Recast the AI bullet to show business value: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy and structured content model to improve content discovery and member self-service.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “digital strategy” repeat heavily from NACo; keep only the version with the clearest new outcome.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a notable result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add clearer outcomes for channels, studio, and analytics work.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most strategic wins first and make verbs more outcome-driven: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen weaker bullets with measurable impact where possible: add email open/click growth, social engagement, video output, event volume, cost savings, reporting speed, or adoption rates.
- Tighten phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting infrastructure.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Video/newsletter leadership overlaps with the prior NACo role; here, emphasize scale, team leadership, and infrastructure rather than recurring production.
- Governance/workflow language also appears elsewhere; make this entry about enterprise transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial operations.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-led: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with ownership: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes with communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing coordination and workflow consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved digital publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Produced and expanded” video content may duplicate the earlier role’s “weekly video updates”; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and outcomes-oriented language rather than broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, workflow design & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & user-centered storytelling
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience: “platform modernization,” “content operations,” and “governance” are better supported than “audience-focused content planning.”
- If space allows, make one item more impact-oriented, e.g. “Digital strategy for large-scale Drupal ecosystems and multi-team publishing environments.”
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets for punch and scannability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also appears multiple times in the summary and work history.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a curated skills statement. It also overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section, so this version should stay higher-level and emphasize recent, differentiating strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems design • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they matter for target roles; otherwise trim to avoid diluting your strongest recent platform experience.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems design” and “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clearer business value.
- Consider dropping one or two older/less central platforms to make the line more senior and focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills strategic, and leave full platform/tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies (“Web & CMS administration”).

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for a senior digital lead, but it reads as a generic keyword list. It would be stronger if framed around business use and decision-making impact, especially since your recent NACo role already proves hands-on analytics leadership.

Suggested edit
- Recast from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Digital analytics strategy, dashboarding, and performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO, UX, and content performance analysis”
- If you can support it elsewhere, add measurable scope in experience bullets rather than here, e.g., reporting for a 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies; “executive dashboards” is more specific.
- Avoid repeating the exact GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery list in multiple sections unless one version adds context.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize broadcast-quality production capability and event formats you’ve led.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, outcome-linked phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera direction and studio operations • Virtual event production workflows”
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than tools alone: “In-house studio production” or “Multi-camera livestream production” is stronger than just “video editing.”
- Consider dropping “virtual event production” or “livestreaming” if both feel repetitive; “livestream and hybrid event delivery” can cover both.
- Keep this item concise since the work history already proves it; use it as a signal, not a full description.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; consider keeping the detailed version here and shortening/removing the core competency mention.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are niche but older-skill coded unless tied to recent in-house studio leadership.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to sharpen relevance and signal level of use, especially Drupal given the recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/current platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise CMS, migration/redesign) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names, e.g. “Drupal (10,000+ page environment)” or “SharePoint (intranet/content admin)” to show applied depth.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was minor compared with enterprise CMS work; replace with a more relevant platform only if used materially.
- Keep wording consistent with the rest of the CV: platform names only or platform + function, not a mix.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “CMS modernization” is already covered elsewhere, so don’t repeat it here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/less central tools unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten phrasing and group by function: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add one or two higher-value specifics tied to recent work: e.g., “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner, more senior positioning unless ATS targeting requires them.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates Topline Skills [2] almost exactly (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”).
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want a developer/DevOps signal.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Operational Systems & Automation.”
- Tighten and group by function: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Teams”
- If accurate, add light proficiency/context instead of just names: “Built workflows in Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier; managed cross-team planning in Jira, Asana, and Trello.”
- Prioritize the strongest/recent tools first; consider dropping weaker or older platforms if they were not central in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack and Teams are standard collaboration tools; keep only if they materially support the workflow/operations story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo roles. It should emphasize enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, newsletter operations, audience engagement)**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — used to support high-volume newsletters, member communications and campaign email operations**
- Keep platform names only if space is tight; otherwise add a short qualifier tied to recent work, not older entry-level experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about newsletters reaching “tens of thousands”; don’t repeat those metrics here unless you remove them elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may partially overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs without repeating later leadership/operations language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Make responsibilities more concrete and concise: “supported web refresh, produced livestreams and weekly advocacy videos, and improved publishing workflows across web, email, and social.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with stronger phrasing if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” overlaps with later operations bullets; keep this entry focused on early buildout and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and first-of-its-kind impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Condense the rest into one supporting clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and research dissemination.”
- If possible, add a measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this broader and more innovation/program-focused.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here since those strengths are better established in 2015–2024 roles.
